note:
FIXTURES, NOT A MODEL. These rows are calibration fixtures pending issue #95, which replaces this lookup table with a roofline model. A single `outputTokensPerSec` per hardware configuration is not a property of the hardware: the measured spread on identical hardware is 24x with concurrency alone (docs/research/2026-10-14-inference-serving-research.md section 10), so every row here is one point on a curve, not a capacity. The point each row records is stated explicitly in `measuredPerUserTokensPerSec`: the throughput sustained while each concurrent user still receives 50 output tokens/s, on a single-turn chat workload of 8,000 input and 1,000 output tokens. Pick a different interactivity target and the same hardware gives a different number -- gpt-oss 120B on one H100 sustains 8,973 total tok/s/GPU at 50 tok/s/user but only 2,558 at 200 tok/s/user, a 3.5x swing with no hardware change.

DERIVATION. `measuredTotalTokensPerSecPerGpu` is the published figure, verbatim, from the `source` URL -- SemiAnalysis InferenceX, which sweeps concurrency on real hardware and publishes the throughput-versus-interactivity frontier. Those figures count TOTAL tokens (input + output): the published $/1M figures divide the $/GPU/hr rate by exactly that number, which is how the denominator was confirmed. On an 8K-in/1K-out workload there are 9 total tokens per output token, so `outputTokensPerSec = round(measuredTotalTokensPerSecPerGpu / 9) * gpuCount`. Nothing here is estimated or interpolated; the only derived quantities are that division and the GPU count.

GPU COUNT. The published figures are per-GPU, so `gpuCount` is chosen as the smallest deployment whose weights fit at the measured precision and vLLM's default 0.90 memory utilization -- the arithmetic is spelled out per row in `gpuCountBasis`. Cost per token is invariant to this choice, because `calculateSelfHostCost` scales both the rental cost and the throughput linearly in `gpuCount`; the count sets the size of the deployment shown, not its economics.

maxConcurrentRequests. Kept only because `SelfHostEntry` (src/data/types.ts:45) requires it; nothing in the engine reads it (`calculateSelfHostCost` ignores it entirely). It is no longer a capacity claim. It now records the concurrency the throughput figure was actually measured at -- `outputTokensPerSec / measuredPerUserTokensPerSec` -- which is the quantity the roofline work in #95 needs, and is only meaningful alongside `measuredInputTokens` + `measuredOutputTokens`. The previous values were capacity assertions at an unstated context length, and the research doc measured them wrong by 1.7x in one direction and 2.5x in the other from the same row. Dropping the field outright is the better end state and needs `maxConcurrentRequests` removed from `SelfHostEntry` first; `tsc -b` rejects its absence today.

THE TWO 8B ROWS ARE A DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT. They are not comparable to the rest of the table and are not from InferenceX. They report output tokens/s directly, measured at a fixed concurrency of 50 on a short workload (~100 input / 600 output) on an RTX Pro 6000 -- so `measuredPerUserTokensPerSec` is null, because that run holds concurrency fixed rather than holding per-user interactivity fixed, and `maxConcurrentRequests` 50 is the measured concurrency rather than a derived one. They are included because the small end is where self-hosting most often beats an API and a menu without it is less useful, not because they belong on the same axis as the rows above. InferenceX's fleet starts at 70B, and no 7-13B benchmark on a datacenter SKU was found that states output tokens/s together with its concurrency and context -- the same source's H100 and A100 comparisons report total throughput only, at unstated sequence lengths, so they could not be converted.

WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHY. No DeepSeek V4/V4.1, GLM 5.x, Kimi K3, MiniMax M3 or Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, although all are benchmarked and all are current. Their runs use the AgentX agentic-coding workload, which is explicitly not a fixed token mix ("thousands of requests across growing conversations, subagents, warmup periods, cache states, and dynamically changing in-flight load"), so their published total-token figures cannot be converted to output tokens/s. Admitting them needs `outputTokensPerSec: number | null` on `SelfHostEntry`, which `tsc -b` rejects today -- a null there fails the build at src/components/InferenceCalculator.tsx:85. No number was invented to fill the gap.

CROSS-CHECK, AND THE SIZE OF THE PROBLEM. An independent vLLM v0.10.2 run of gpt-oss-120b on 2x H100 SXM reports 7,648.67 OUTPUT tok/s on a ShareGPT workload (https://docs.gpustack.ai/latest/performance-lab/gpt-oss-120b/h100/). The two H100 rows here total 1,994. Both are correct: ShareGPT runs to saturation with no latency target, these rows hold 50 tok/s/user. The 3.8x gap between two honest measurements of the same model on the same hardware is the single best argument for #95.

PAIRING. src/data/cloud-gpu-pricing.json is still at 2026-06-01 and prices only H100 and A100, so the H200, B200 and MI355X rows here have no matching instance to cost against until that file is refreshed (section 8.1 of the research doc has the vendor-verified rates).
